Investigating specific stressors, stereotypic behaviors, and slaughter conditions is critical to establishing comprehensive welfare standards that go beyond basic health and nutrition.

claim: Researchers need to design, implement, and empirically test public health frameworks aimed at mitigating harms arising from modern digital gambling and emerging technologies.
grounds: The abstract concludes that 'The development and testing of a public health approach to addressing the harms associated with gambling in these areas is needed.'
warrant: As digital gambling becomes more integrated into daily life, individual-focused responsible gambling measures are insufficient, requiring systemic, population-level public health interventions to effectively reduce harm.

claim: Prior research on masstige marketing is methodologically limited, lacking diverse approaches such as experimental designs and mixed-method research.
grounds: The abstract highlights the need to 'suggest diverse approaches, that is, mixed and experimental methods (Methodology)' to advance the field.
warrant: Relying primarily on survey-based correlational data limits the ability to establish causal relationships between masstige marketing strategies and consumer behavior, which experimental and mixed-method designs can resolve.

claim: Developing hybrid human-in-the-loop workflows and error-detection mechanisms to mitigate the risk of false negatives (wrongly discarded papers) caused by the 12% error rate of the LLM.
grounds: the overall accuracy of ChatGPT for article discarding and classification is 88%, and (2) the F-1 scores of ChatGPT for article discarding and classification are 91% and 88%, respectively, compared to expert assessments.
warrant: In systematic reviews, missing relevant literature can introduce publication bias and invalidate the review's conclusions, meaning the current 88% accuracy must be supplemented with verification protocols to ensure scientific rigor.

claim: There is a lack of empirical validation and comparative studies on the effectiveness of different unstructured data integration methods in real-world process mining applications.
grounds: The abstract highlights that 'there is no empirical overview on how unstructured data is leveraged in process mining.'
warrant: Without empirical evaluations, practitioners cannot assess the reliability, accuracy, and scalability of methods that extract process data from unstructured sources, hindering industry adoption.

claim: Empirical evaluation of the methodological and reporting quality of published scoping reviews using established assessment frameworks.
grounds: The abstract notes, 'We did not identify any... studies that assessed the quality of scoping review reporting.'
warrant: Assessing the quality of existing reviews is necessary to identify common reporting deficiencies, track improvements over time, and guide peer reviewers and editors in maintaining high scientific standards.

claim: There is a lack of empirical research evaluating the effectiveness of specific pedagogical interventions and curriculum designs in improving postgraduate students' literature review skills.
grounds: The abstract highlights that 'many postgraduate students in higher education institutions lack the necessary skills and understanding to conduct in-depth literature reviews.'
warrant: Identifying effective teaching methodologies is critical to systematically resolve student skill deficiencies and prevent biased or incorrect inferences in academic theses.

claim: There is a lack of a universally validated, cross-culturally tested measurement scale for digital leadership.
grounds: The abstract identifies 'the development of digital leadership scale within diverse contexts' as a primary ongoing research topic.
warrant: Without a standardized and cross-culturally validated scale, empirical findings cannot be reliably compared across different global regions, limiting the generalizability of digital leadership theories.

claim: There is a lack of empirical research on how documented data regarding attacks on healthcare is practically utilized for advocacy, protection, and accountability.
grounds: The abstract states that 'practical questions on how the data is utilized for advocacy, protection and accountability must be prioritized.'
warrant: Resolving this gap is critical to ensure that data collection efforts translate into actionable policies, legal accountability, and improved safety measures for healthcare workers in conflict zones.

claim: There is a lack of advanced, predictive, or inferential quantitative analysis methods used to evaluate project success data.
grounds: Questionnaire, interview and case study have comprised the main data collection methods, and descriptive data analysis was performed in most of the case/field studies.
warrant: Relying primarily on descriptive statistics limits the ability to establish statistical significance, model complex interactions, or build predictive frameworks for project success.

claim: Current service robot literature lacks integration with technical disciplines such as computer science, engineering, and information systems.
grounds: The authors state as a limitation that 'Our review focused on the business and service literature. Future work may want to include additional literature streams, including those in computer science, engineering and information systems.'
warrant: Bridging business research with technical disciplines ensures that service robot design and engineering are aligned with human-centric service requirements and organizational strategies, rather than developing technology in isolation.

claim: Future research needs to investigate the impact of drug reminder packaging on humanistic outcomes, such as patient satisfaction and health-related quality of life.
grounds: The abstract explicitly highlights 'missing humanistic... outcomes' as an important gap limiting firm conclusions.
warrant: Evaluating humanistic outcomes is essential to understand the patient's perspective and ensure that the packaging design actually improves their daily living experience and treatment satisfaction, which are key drivers of long-term adherence.

claim: There is a lack of empirical research exploring the learning outcomes of less frequently utilized gameplay modes (such as collaborative or multiplayer modes) and diverse game genres in primary mathematics.
grounds: The abstract notes that the review analyzed and highlighted the 'types of games and gaming modes frequently utilized for elementary school children'.
warrant: Investigating diverse gameplay modes is essential to understand how social interaction and different game mechanics influence student engagement, collaboration skills, and mathematical conceptual understanding.

claim: Optimal diagnostic imaging pathways and acute management strategies for patients presenting with traumatic brain injury (TBI) and concurrent vascular injuries remain unresolved.
grounds: The abstract highlights that 'Research questions related to traumatic brain injury, vascular injury... were highly prioritized' by the Delphi panel.
warrant: TBI and vascular trauma are primary drivers of preventable death and long-term disability; resolving these gaps will streamline emergency interventions and improve neurofunctional outcomes.

claim: There is a lack of empirical validation demonstrating that adherence to the proposed SLR guidelines directly correlates with lower rejection rates or higher citation impact for newly written reviews.
grounds: The authors propose guidelines to address the problem where 'a lot of review articles are rejected or fail to create a significant impact,' but do not test the efficacy of their proposed guidelines.
warrant: Without empirical testing of the guidelines' impact on actual publication outcomes, it remains unproven whether these specific recommendations successfully resolve the high rejection rates and low impact identified in the problem statement.

claim: Longitudinal research is required to establish a direct causal link between the adoption of specific sustainability practices and the long-term financial performance and multigenerational survival of family firms.
grounds: The abstract emphasizes that "Underscoring the critical role of sustainability in attaining long-term success becomes essential for these firms."
warrant: Family firms are characterized by a transgenerational outlook, but literature reviews cannot empirically prove whether sustainability initiatives directly extend the lifespan or improve the financial resilience of these firms over generations.

claim: A comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis that incorporates non-English publications and multiple databases (such as PubMed and Web of Science) to mitigate publication and database bias.
grounds: A literature search was performed utilizing the Scopus® database, employing keywords pertaining to BE to analyze papers published in English from 1990 to 2023.
warrant: Relying solely on Scopus and English-language papers may omit critical regional epidemiological data on causative pathogens, resistance patterns, and treatment outcomes, limiting the global applicability of the findings.

claim: There is a lack of research investigating the combined dynamics and feedbacks between coastal eutrophication pressures and ecosystem impacts.
grounds: few studies investigate pressures and impacts together, indicating that feedbacks are understudied.
warrant: Understanding these feedbacks is essential for predicting ecosystem responses to management actions and avoiding unintended ecological consequences.

claim: Specific auditing standards and verification methodologies for real-time, large-scale big data analytics in sustainability reporting have not yet been established.
grounds: The abstract emphasizes the urgency of developing 'robust assurance mechanisms' for BDA-driven sustainability accounting.
warrant: Traditional static auditing techniques cannot effectively verify the continuous, high-volume data streams used in BDA, leaving ESG disclosures vulnerable to greenwashing and data manipulation without specialized assurance frameworks.

claim: There is a lack of empirical case studies and actionable frameworks demonstrating the practical realization and execution of Sustainable Industry 4.0 initiatives in real-world manufacturing environments.
grounds: The abstract notes that 'many papers do not provide an insight into realization of initiatives to introduce Sustainable Industry 4.0.'
warrant: Without concrete implementation pathways and empirical evidence of success, organizations lack the practical guidance needed to transition from theoretical sustainability concepts to operational reality.

claim: There is a lack of integrated socio-ecological frameworks that combine agro-ecological performance data with socio-economic behavioral models to explain the 'why' behind smallholder farmer decisions to adopt or reject Conservation Agriculture.
grounds: The abstract states that the literature represents two distinct approaches (agro-ecological and socio-economic) and that 'neither of these approaches can address the full scope of this question, in particular its ‘why’ component' regarding farmer decision-making.
warrant: Resolving this gap is critical because understanding the biophysical benefits of Conservation Agriculture is insufficient if researchers cannot explain the socio-economic drivers and constraints that influence actual farmer adoption in diverse contexts.

claim: There is a lack of longitudinal research tracking how digital leadership capabilities and dimensions adapt over time in response to rapid, disruptive technological paradigm shifts.
grounds: The abstract highlights 'dynamic adaptation' as a key characteristic and 'digital change' as a core dimension of digital leadership.
warrant: Cross-sectional studies and literature reviews cannot capture the temporal, long-term evolution of leadership adaptation during continuous technological disruption, which requires resource-intensive longitudinal tracking.

claim: Future research must empirically assess the long-term impact of the PRISMA-ScR checklist on the actual reporting quality and methodological transparency of published scoping reviews post-implementation.
grounds: The authors note that 'methodological and reporting quality needs to improve' and that reporting guidelines are intended to increase transparency, but the paper only covers the development and initial testing of the checklist.
warrant: The creation of a reporting guideline does not automatically translate to improved literature quality. Longitudinal bibliometric analyses are necessary to determine if the guideline is being adopted and if its adoption correlates with measurable improvements in reporting completeness.

claim: Pivoting traditional text mining techniques to leverage retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and LLM agents for automated mining of unstructured software repositories (MSR) and developer chat logs.
grounds: Stagnant concept 'text mining' has a temporal decay rate of 0.56, indicating a 56% decline in new research activity connected to it in recent years.
warrant: Traditional text mining relies on static NLP techniques (like TF-IDF or basic NER) which fail to capture semantic context in modern developer communications (e.g., Slack, Discord). Integrating LLMs and RAG into text mining pipelines revives the field by enabling deep semantic understanding of unstructured developer discussions, mapping them to code changes with higher accuracy.

claim: Research is needed to explore the integration and interoperability of these distinct technology clusters (such as RFID, CAD, and Industry 4.0) across the entire apparel supply chain.
grounds: The abstract identifies six distinct clusters of prevalent research trends (including RFID, virtual-try on, CAD, and Industry 4.0) and calls for research on 'trends in the apparel supply chain'.
warrant: While existing literature studies these technologies in isolated clusters, understanding their end-to-end integration is crucial for achieving seamless data flow, supply chain visibility, and operational efficiency in the apparel industry.

claim: Future research needs to investigate methods to overcome data sharing constraints and limited data accessibility in supply chain management, such as through federated learning or privacy-preserving data sharing protocols.
grounds: The main gaps found in the shortlisted studies are limited data accessibility
warrant: AI and ML models require large, diverse, and high-quality datasets to train effectively; resolving data accessibility issues is critical to deploying robust, real-world predictive models across supply chain partners.

claim: There is a lack of research examining corporate risk disclosure practices within developing countries, private institutions, and non-profit organizations.
grounds: The findings also indicate that limited studies focus on developing countries, private institutions, and non-profit organizations.
warrant: Investigating these underrepresented contexts is essential because their unique regulatory environments, stakeholder demands, and governance structures differ significantly from public companies in developed nations, meaning existing risk disclosure models may not be generalizable to them.

claim: The specific methodological approaches and contextual research agendas proposed by the study remain unexecuted and require empirical application.
grounds: The authors state that they 'provide future research directions, contexts and methodology' based on the identified gaps.
warrant: Proposing future directions only identifies the path forward; actual execution of these methodologies (e.g., longitudinal studies or experimental designs) is necessary to resolve the field's theoretical fragmentation.

claim: There is insufficient research on landscape-scale changes caused by mining and the development of early-warning ecological indicators in the Amazon.
grounds: The abstract notes that environmental monitoring & impact indicators, disease hotspots, and landscape changes due to resource extraction were the least represented, revealing limited attention to broader-scale ecological processes and early-warning indicators.
warrant: Understanding broad-scale landscape dynamics is critical for regional conservation planning and preventing irreversible ecosystem degradation before it occurs.

claim: Research must expand the application of AI and ML to under-explored supply chain management domains beyond demand forecasting and risk management, such as procurement, inventory optimization, and logistics.
grounds: The limitations of the study are the review size and the scope of AI and ML applications in SCM.
warrant: A supply chain is an interconnected system, and focusing intelligent automation only on forecasting and risk management leaves other critical operational areas unoptimized, limiting overall supply chain efficiency.

claim: Implementing automated mechanisms to detect, reconcile, and weight contradictory or conflicting pharmacogenomic claims across a rapidly expanding corpus.
grounds: The abstract highlights the double-exponential growth of Medline, requiring automated systems to continually update and generate a comprehensive view of pharmacogenomic knowledge.
warrant: The exponential growth of literature inevitably introduces conflicting findings due to differing study designs or populations. A system that merely extracts relations without resolving contradictions will generate unreliable knowledge maps.

claim: The current understanding of agricultural sustainability trends is limited by database selection bias, leaving grey literature, regional databases, and non-English scientific publications unexamined.
grounds: The study's corpus was limited to '3302 bibliographic records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, which was selected because of its standardized metadata structure'.
warrant: Relying solely on Web of Science may overlook localized agroecological innovations, regional policy reports, and practitioner-led assessments that are not published in mainstream English-language journals but are critical for understanding global sustainability transitions.

claim: There is a need for targeted empirical research on the health vulnerabilities and healthcare access of highly under-studied migrant subgroups, specifically cross-border patients and migrant workers.
grounds: The abstract notes that only '26 (0.1%) [documents] were about patients’ mobility across international borders' and '1328 (6.2%) were about migrant workers'.
warrant: Aggregating all migrants into broad categories obscures the unique legal, occupational, and medical challenges faced by specific subgroups, preventing the development of targeted health interventions for highly vulnerable populations like migrant laborers.

claim: Empirical validation and practical application of the proposed three-domain framework (circular product, process, and platform) in real-world construction projects.
grounds: The abstract states that 'A new framework for CE implementation is proposed to support critical discussion and identification of future research trajectories... The framework identifies three innovation domains: circular product, circular process, and circular platform.'
warrant: Because the framework is derived from a systematic literature review, it remains theoretical. Empirical testing is required to prove its viability and effectiveness in overcoming the construction industry's conservative and fragmented nature.

claim: TAM needs to be applied to evaluate the acceptance of emerging technologies like 5G, AI, cloud computing, AR, VR, and BYOD in higher education settings.
grounds: Future technologies such as 5G, AI, cloud computing, augmented reality, virtual reality, and BYOD represent new TAM-related research gaps.
warrant: As higher education institutions adopt advanced digital tools, understanding how users accept these complex, modern technologies is essential to guide effective implementation strategies.

claim: There is a lack of research investigating the adoption, implementation, and effectiveness of non-financial reporting formats within public healthcare organizations.
grounds: The abstract explicitly states that the existing literature has remained 'silent on the healthcare sector' concerning non-financial reporting formats.
warrant: Public healthcare organizations have distinct operational models, stakeholder expectations, and clinical governance structures compared to local governments or universities, requiring tailored non-financial reporting insights to improve accountability and service delivery.

claim: The development and implementation of integrated, multi-disciplinary complex decision-making frameworks that combine MCDM with structural and environmental simulation tools.
grounds: The abstract notes that 'there is luck [lack] of complex problem solving approach in cultural heritage buildings area.'
warrant: Heritage conservation involves highly complex, interdependent variables (e.g., structural integrity vs. historical aesthetics) that standard MCDM methods alone cannot resolve without integration with physical simulation and complex systems modeling.

claim: The study does not systematically categorize or analyze the specific ethical, legal, and technical challenges (such as hallucinations, data privacy, and bias) associated with implementing responsible GenAI in medicine.
grounds: While emphasizing the transformative impact of LLMs in healthcare, it also highlights the necessity of responsible GenAI applications.
warrant: Simply highlighting the necessity of responsible AI is insufficient; researchers and policymakers need a structured taxonomy of the specific risks and mitigation strategies currently discussed in the literature to establish safe deployment guidelines.

claim: Future systematic reviews should conduct a full-text analysis of 100% of the sampled literature to prevent selection bias and ensure comprehensive typology mapping.
grounds: The abstract mentions characterizing organizations 'after reading 68% of the articles', leaving a portion of the literature unexamined for typology.
warrant: Partial reading of a literature sample can lead to incomplete categorization, potentially omitting critical niche startup characteristics or emerging business models present in the unread 32% of the papers.

claim: The analysis is limited to a single database (Scopus), potentially omitting relevant computer science preprints or specialized medical literature.
grounds: A total of 3,941 academic publications related to the use of LLMs in medicine were retrieved from the Scopus database...
warrant: Medical AI is a rapidly evolving, interdisciplinary field where critical technical breakthroughs are often published first on preprint servers or in specialized engineering databases, meaning a single-source database search may yield an incomplete picture of the research landscape.

claim: There is a lack of theoretically-grounded, generalizable, and quantitative empirical studies investigating entrepreneurship in the rural hospitality and tourism (RHT) sector.
grounds: The content analysis revealed different gaps and limitations in the understanding of entrepreneurship in RHT, including a predominance of qualitative studies with limited theoretically-grounded and generalizable empirical studies.
warrant: Relying heavily on qualitative research limits the ability to generalize findings and establish causal relationships. Conducting rigorous quantitative and theoretically-grounded empirical studies is necessary to validate existing frameworks and provide scalable insights for policymakers and practitioners.

claim: There is a need for future studies to employ diverse and underutilized methodological approaches, such as longitudinal designs, action research, and mixed-methods, to study SBM in HEIs.
grounds: The abstract highlights the "ongoing existence of... methodological preferences" in the current literature on SBM in HEIs.
warrant: Over-reliance on specific methodological preferences limits the depth and generalizability of findings; employing diverse methodologies is necessary to capture the long-term, dynamic impacts of sustainability initiatives within complex institutional settings.

claim: The performance and adaptability of the Python toolkit must be tested and validated across other diverse scientific domains beyond food science and cold denaturation.
grounds: The method was evaluated using a specific 'dataset of 6102 publications about cold denaturation' as a case study.
warrant: Without cross-domain validation, it remains unproven whether the toolkit's performance (especially its high recall of 0.949) holds true for fields with different terminologies, publication volumes, and writing styles.

claim: There is a need to analyze ostrich welfare literature indexed in alternative databases (such as Web of Science, PubMed, or Google Scholar) and include non-English publications.
grounds: The study states that 'a literature exploration was achieved using the Scopus® database' and only 'Papers distributed in the English language from 1983 to 2023 were included.'
warrant: Restricting the systematic review to Scopus and English-only papers likely excludes significant regional research from major ostrich-farming nations where findings may be published in local languages or indexed in different databases, resulting in an incomplete global picture of ostrich welfare practices.

claim: There is a need to investigate non-financial reporting formats other than sustainability reporting, such as integrated reporting or popular reporting, in public sector contexts.
grounds: The abstract notes that 'most existing studies have focused on sustainability reporting,' while public sector organizations adopt 'different reporting formats... to report various dimensions of their performance.'
warrant: Public sector performance is multi-dimensional, and focusing predominantly on sustainability reporting overlooks how other formats can communicate public value, intellectual capital, and operational efficiency to stakeholders.

claim: There is an absence of clear guidelines on the optimal timing and safety profiles for initiating venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis in patients with severe pelvic fractures.
grounds: The abstract explicitly identifies 'pelvic fracture, and venous thromboembolism prophylaxis' as areas with highly prioritized, unanswered research questions.
warrant: Pelvic fractures carry a high risk of both massive hemorrhage and subsequent thromboembolic events, making the timing of anticoagulation a critical clinical dilemma that directly impacts patient survival.

claim: The integration and evaluation of emerging technologies, such as large language models and automated screening tools, in the scientific literature review process remains unexplored.
grounds: The abstract prompts 'established scholars to explore more innovative ways through which scientific literature reviews can be conducted'.
warrant: Investigating these innovative technological approaches is essential to address the scalability challenges of manual literature reviews and to minimize human bias in selection and synthesis.

claim: There is a need to develop stochastic and robust optimization models for asset prepositioning that simultaneously account for uncertainties in funding, supply availability, and infrastructure integrity.
grounds: The abstract explicitly states that there is a lack of papers that 'deal with uncertainty in funding, budget, asset and supply quantities, and infrastructure' in the context of disaster prepositioning.
warrant: Disaster environments are highly volatile; failing to model these uncertainties can lead to unrealistic prepositioning strategies that fail during actual operations due to budget shortfalls or damaged transport networks.

claim: Future research needs to develop and evaluate topic modeling architectures that integrate statistical uncertainty quantification methods, such as conformal prediction, to validate the identified gaps.
grounds: Furthermore, future studies could evaluate more efficient modeling algorithms, especially those combining topic modeling with statistical uncertainty quantification, such as conformal prediction.
warrant: Traditional topic modeling algorithms cluster documents heuristically without providing statistical guarantees, meaning that incorporating uncertainty quantification is necessary to establish confidence levels and reduce false positives in the identified research gaps.

claim: A systematic investigation into the less common, novel, or population-specific genetic variants causing NSHL and SHL in the Saudi population is required.
grounds: It also sheds light on areas where further research is needed to fully understand the genetic foundations of hearing loss in the Saudi population.
warrant: The Saudi population has a unique genetic structure due to high rates of consanguinity, meaning standard global genetic panels may miss population-specific variants crucial for accurate diagnosis.

claim: The longitudinal effects of smart factory adoption on employee engagement and operational efficiency over time are not addressed.
grounds: The abstract notes that the study 'addresses previously unexplored relationships among training, workplace support and operational efficiency' to 'ensure sustainable competitiveness' but does not measure these over time.
warrant: Since technology adoption is a multi-stage process, cross-sectional frameworks cannot capture how employee engagement, training needs, and workplace support requirements evolve as smart factory technologies transition from novelty to routine operations.

claim: There is a lack of empirical research establishing the direct causal mechanisms and quantitative relationships between specific fish welfare indicators and the reduction of antimicrobial use (AMU) and antimicrobial resistance (AR) in aquaculture.
grounds: The abstract explicitly notes that the analysis highlighted 'areas that require further investigation, such as the link between these research fields [fish welfare and AMU/AR]'.
warrant: Without identifying which specific welfare improvements (e.g., reduced stocking density, environmental enrichment) directly minimize the need for antimicrobials, aquaculture producers cannot implement targeted, cost-effective welfare interventions to mitigate AR.

claim: There is a gap in empirical justice health research focusing on the specific healthcare, psychological, and rehabilitative needs of individuals convicted of sex offenses and crimes relating to children.
grounds: The abstract notes that 'Those convicted of sex offenses and crimes relating to children were not as researched as the existing literature suggests, with a focus instead on populations with mental illness...'
warrant: Failing to study these specific offender groups limits the development of targeted, evidence-based interventions and risk-management strategies necessary for their rehabilitation and successful reintegration into society.

claim: The study maps publication trends but does not assess the actual clinical validation, safety, or deployment readiness of the LLM applications described in the literature.
grounds: BERTopic method... is used to analyze and classify publications on LLMs applications in medicine. The findings show that LLMs are mostly concentrated in the fields of radiology, ophthalmology and mental health...
warrant: Identifying that LLMs are frequently discussed in radiology or mental health does not translate to clinical utility; research must evaluate the transition from academic publication to real-world clinical efficacy and safety.

claim: There is a lack of comparative studies evaluating the therapeutic bio-equivalence and standardization of complex functional foods and crude plant extracts versus purified, single-active-ingredient nutraceuticals in managing canine leishmaniosis.
grounds: The abstract identifies 'Functional food effects' and 'Extract effects' as key research areas but emphasizes the overall scarcity of literature ('only a few studies on this issue so far').
warrant: Crude extracts and functional foods have highly variable compositions, making it difficult to guarantee consistent therapeutic outcomes; comparative studies are necessary to identify which specific compounds drive clinical improvement and to standardize formulations for veterinary use.

claim: There is a need to evaluate and validate the applicability, usability, and effectiveness of the PRISMA-ScR checklist in non-health disciplines, such as social sciences, engineering, or education.
grounds: The abstract states that the PRISMA-ScR checklist was tested by workshop participants applying it 'to a scoping review on a health-related topic.'
warrant: Scoping reviews are conducted across a wide range of heterogeneous disciplines. Restricting the initial testing to a health-related topic leaves it unclear whether the checklist items are fully compatible with the diverse methodological traditions and reporting needs of other fields.

claim: There is a shortage of corporate governance research focusing on financial institutions, such as banks and insurance companies, in the Malaysian market.
grounds: The abstract notes that prior studies 'were carried out using archived data from non-financial firms'.
warrant: Financial firms are subject to distinct regulatory requirements and systemic risk profiles, meaning that corporate governance models derived from non-financial firms may not be applicable or effective for them.

claim: The development of an integrated conceptual framework linking business intelligence and big data to hospitality and tourism management.
grounds: A conceptual framework that helps to identify critical business problems and links the domains of business intelligence and big data to tourism and hospitality management and development is missing.
warrant: A unified framework is necessary to guide researchers and practitioners in systematically identifying and solving critical business problems using data-driven approaches rather than relying on fragmented, ad-hoc applications.

claim: The integration and evaluation of automated machine learning (AutoML) frameworks within R-based energy forecasting workflows remain largely unexplored.
grounds: Notably, few studies incorporated automated model selection...
warrant: Non-specialists face significant technical barriers in manual hyperparameter tuning and model selection. Developing standardized R-based AutoML pipelines is essential to lower the barrier to entry and ensure optimal forecasting performance without requiring deep AI expertise.

claim: There is currently no globally accepted, standardized, and harmonized physical activity measurement instrument for children and adolescents.
grounds: The development of a new PA measurement instrument that would be globally accepted and harmonized is a global health priority to help improve the accuracy and reliability of global surveillance.
warrant: A unified, globally accepted instrument is necessary to eliminate methodological discrepancies, allowing for accurate, reliable, and comparable global surveillance data.

claim: Future empirical research must investigate sustainable business management (SBM) practices in HEIs located in underrepresented geographical regions, particularly in developing economies and the Global South.
grounds: The abstract explicitly notes the "ongoing existence of... geographical imbalances" within the analyzed corpus of empirical literature on sustainable business management (SBM) in higher education institutions (HEIs).
warrant: Resolving geographical imbalances is critical because sustainability challenges, funding structures, and institutional capacities vary widely across different regions, meaning that SBM frameworks developed in dominant regions may not be universally applicable or effective.

claim: Alternative advanced natural language processing techniques, such as transformer-based embeddings or semantic search, need to be evaluated against the LDA and keyword-based approach.
grounds: The study employs 'a combination of latent Dirichlet allocation and food keyword searches' to analyze the dataset.
warrant: LDA and keyword searches are limited by vocabulary matching and do not capture deep semantic relationships, which likely contributes to the low precision rate of the current methodology.

claim: There is a need to update the evidence map to include literature published after early 2020 to capture the evolving landscape of COVID-19 risk and protective factors.
grounds: The methodology specifies, 'We applied this protocol to reports within the COVID-19 Open Research Dataset (CORD-19) that were published in early 2020.'
warrant: Data from early 2020 does not account for subsequent developments such as viral mutations, the introduction of vaccines, therapeutic advancements, and long-term clinical outcomes, which significantly alter susceptibility and risk profiles.

claim: Research needs to address the synergies, trade-offs, and socio-economic incentives associated with implementing diverse solutions for cross-scale coastal eutrophication management.
grounds: few studies investigate synergies, trade-offs and incentives for various solutions to address cross-scale multi-solution management.
warrant: Managing eutrophication effectively requires coordinated, multi-scale actions, which are only viable if decision-makers understand the conflicts, co-benefits, and motivational factors for stakeholders.

claim: There is a lack of comparative guidelines and decision frameworks to help researchers choose between SLRs and other review methodologies (such as scoping reviews, meta-analyses, or narrative reviews) during the planning phase.
grounds: The abstract states that 'The systematic literature review (SLR) is one of the important review methodologies' and focuses exclusively on explaining and providing guidelines for the SLR methodology.
warrant: Without clear comparative frameworks, researchers may default to SLRs when alternative review methodologies are more appropriate for their specific research questions, leading to methodological misalignment and potential rejection.

claim: There is a need to investigate the complex, cascading socio-economic and environmental feedback effects of extreme weather events on human-environment systems.
grounds: The abstract mentions that 'There are still significant study gaps in the fields of the effects of extreme weather events' and highlights concerns over 'goods safety, social safety, and financial losses'.
warrant: Understanding the coupled human-environmental impacts is necessary to prevent systemic failures in food security, social safety, and economic stability, which cannot be addressed by studying physical hazards in isolation.

claim: There is a lack of research integrating environmental monitoring indicators with toxicological pathways and biodiversity assessments in the context of Amazonian mining.
grounds: The co-occurrence–based dissimilarity analysis revealed weak connections among several topic pairs and highlighted substantial gaps, particularly the infrequent association between monitoring indicators and either toxicological or biodiversity-focused studies.
warrant: Linking monitoring indicators directly to toxicological and biodiversity outcomes is essential for creating predictive, early-warning frameworks that protect ecosystem health and human populations.

claim: The formulation of standardized, actionable guidelines and maturity models for establishing a complete and conclusive megaproject management system.
grounds: There are no clear guidelines for achieving a complete and conclusive project management system and enhancing future megaprojects' management capabilities.
warrant: Without standardized guidelines, project managers lack a benchmark to assess and build organizational capabilities, leading to inconsistent practices and repeated mistakes across different megaprojects.

claim: There is a shortage of empirical studies investigating consumer financial behaviors, ethical implications, and regulatory frameworks surrounding AI application in non-banking sectors like insurance and pensions.
grounds: More empirical research is required, especially focusing on consumers' financial behaviors as well as the role of regulation, ethics and policy concerned with AI in financial service contexts, such as insurance or pensions.
warrant: Insurance and pensions involve long-term risk management and sensitive personal data, making it critical to understand how AI-driven decisions affect consumer trust, equity, and compliance with evolving financial regulations.

claim: There is a lack of comparative evaluation comparing this double-thresholding co-occurrence method against alternative automated gap detection approaches, such as deep learning-based semantic embeddings or generative AI.
grounds: The authors describe this work as 'our first approach in automated identification of feasible research gaps by using a double-threshold procedure'.
warrant: Without benchmarking against alternative NLP and network analysis methods, it is impossible to determine the relative accuracy, recall, and computational efficiency of the proposed double-thresholding technique.

claim: There is a lack of research focusing on the performance impacts of standardizing or adapting individual marketing mix elements and their specific effects on customer-related outcomes.
grounds: The abstract identifies research gaps related to individual marketing mix elements, and customer-related performance outcomes (characteristics).
warrant: Broadly assessing marketing programs as a whole obscures the distinct contributions of individual elements (like pricing or distribution), and ignoring customer-centric metrics (like loyalty or satisfaction) limits our understanding of the mechanisms driving overall financial performance.

claim: Integrating formal systematic methods (such as automated model checking and program synthesis constraints) directly into LLM-based code generation pipelines to guarantee semantic correctness.
grounds: The stagnant concept 'systematic methods' has a temporal decay rate of 0.67, indicating a 67% decline in new research activity and connections in the literature graph over recent years.
warrant: Modern generative AI tools produce code rapidly but lack correctness guarantees, leading to security vulnerabilities. Reviving systematic methods by embedding them as verification layers in LLM pipelines ensures generated code adheres to formal specifications without requiring manual proof construction.

claim: The generalizability of the framework to other manufacturing sectors or different geographical and cultural contexts remains unexplored.
grounds: The title and abstract focus specifically on the 'Sri Lankan Apparel Sector' and 'apparel manufacturing'.
warrant: Smart factory implementations and employee dynamics vary significantly across different industries and countries due to varying labor laws, cultural dimensions, and technological maturity, meaning the framework may not apply universally without modification.

claim: The framework lacks an empirical evaluation of how human-AI interaction affects the objectivity of the literature review and whether it introduces algorithmic bias or cognitive overhead for the researcher.
grounds: The framework consists of several steps in which the critical mind of the scientist is supported by machine learning.
warrant: If the machine learning algorithms prioritize certain terms or topics incorrectly, they may bias the researcher's selection process, thereby compromising the validity and comprehensiveness of the literature review.

claim: There is insufficient research on the trade-offs and optimal balance between AI-driven automation for operational efficiency and the preservation of human-centric hospitality in personalized travel experiences.
grounds: The abstract notes that AI transforms tourism by 'augmenting customer service, improving operational efficiency, personalizing travel experiences'.
warrant: Because tourism is inherently a high-touch industry, over-automating services to cut costs may degrade the customer experience, requiring researchers to define the boundaries where AI augmentation begins to diminish perceived service quality.

claim: Investigating dynamic, real-time science mapping mechanisms that can automatically update and predict emerging scientific trends from streaming publication data.
grounds: The abstract notes that the study 'sheds light on previously unexplored mechanisms in the literature of bibliometric analysis, revealing gaps in existing research.'
warrant: Traditional bibliometric analysis is static and retrospective; developing real-time, predictive mapping mechanisms is essential for proactive policymaking and funding allocation, though it presents high technical complexity in data streaming and predictive modeling.

claim: There is a need to investigate the specific communication frameworks, reporting standards, and disclosure strategies that family firms can employ to minimize information asymmetry regarding their sustainability practices.
grounds: The abstract highlights that "Given their pivotal role in the business market, it is crucial to effectively communicate this commitment [to sustainability] to the general public, regulators and investors."
warrant: Family firms have unique governance structures and stakeholder relationships; understanding how they can effectively signal their sustainability efforts is critical to securing external investment and maintaining public trust.

claim: An empirical investigation into how specific social and cultural factors influence the adoption and acceptance of digital payment methods across different regions.
grounds: The key limitation of the existing theories is their inability to consider the role of social and cultural facets in the adoption of new technology.
warrant: Payment behaviors are deeply embedded in local societal norms and cultural practices, meaning that technology-centric models without social and cultural dimensions fail to accurately predict adoption in diverse global markets.

claim: Future research needs to explore the determinants of corporate governance adoption or its impact on non-financial outcomes such as corporate social responsibility (CSR), risk management, and ethical compliance.
grounds: The abstract highlights that 'the existing literature has primarily focused on the outcomes of CG, especially firm performance'.
warrant: Broadening the scope beyond financial performance is essential to understand how corporate governance reforms drive sustainability, accountability, and long-term stakeholder value in alignment with updated Malaysian CG codes.

claim: Future studies should focus on developing, implementing, and benchmarking deep learning architectures and hybrid AI/ML models tailored for complex supply chain tasks.
grounds: and the need for employing deep and hybrid models.
warrant: Standard regression and basic neural networks may fail to capture the highly non-linear, dynamic, and multi-dimensional relationships in supply chain data, whereas hybrid and deep models can significantly improve forecasting accuracy and risk mitigation.

claim: Evaluating the generalizability and performance of the proposed ChatGPT-based systematic review methodology across diverse scientific domains, such as clinical medicine or qualitative social sciences.
grounds: To illustrate the practical application of our method, we have chosen the topic of IoT applications in water and wastewater management and quality monitoring due to its critical importance and the dearth of comprehensive reviews in this field.
warrant: Different fields have distinct reporting standards, vocabulary complexities, and review methodologies; testing the framework on other domains is necessary to prove its universal utility and identify domain-specific limitations.

claim: There is a lack of established methodologies and collaborative frameworks that successfully integrate Information Systems research with clinical medicine, public health, and medical informatics.
grounds: The abstract concludes by stating: 'We advocate for IS researchers to collaborate more closely with related fields to stay at the forefront of advancements.'
warrant: Without structured interdisciplinary collaboration, IS research risks producing theoretical models that lack clinical validity, failing to address real-world medical regulations, and limiting the practical efficacy of digital health interventions.

claim: There is a lack of research integrating code smell identification tools directly with automated smell removal and bug prediction mechanisms.
grounds: The abstract states that developers strongly associate smell identification with smell removal and bug incidence, but current research only partially addresses these representations.
warrant: Resolving this gap is crucial because developers prioritize the practical outcomes of identification (removal and bug prevention); aligning research with these outcomes will increase the adoption of smell identification tools.

claim: There is a lack of concrete methodological guidelines, procedural steps, and quality assessment criteria for executing the newly proposed 'interpretive sensemaking' review type.
grounds: The authors propose the interpretive sensemaking review as a novel review type rooted in the interpretive paradigm.
warrant: Because this review type is introduced as novel and rooted in the interpretive paradigm, researchers require explicit standards and heuristics to ensure rigor and minimize subjective bias when synthesizing literature through this lens.

claim: There is a lack of geographical diversity in RHT entrepreneurship research, specifically a shortage of studies focusing on non-European contexts.
grounds: Furthermore, a high concentration of studies is from European countries.
warrant: Rural environments, cultural norms, economic conditions, and institutional support systems vary significantly across global regions. Researching non-European contexts is essential to determine if European-centric findings are globally applicable or if unique regional dynamics exist.

claim: Research on the application, challenges, and impacts of artificial intelligence in the back-office and operational environments of financial institutions is underdeveloped.
grounds: The review focuses on AI in customer-facing financial services. Future work may want to investigate back-office and operations contexts.
warrant: While customer-facing AI impacts user experience, back-office AI drives risk assessment, fraud detection, and operational efficiency, which are critical to the systemic stability and security of financial institutions.

claim: Future research needs to move beyond basic, immediate firm-level financial characteristics to explore alternative determinants and consequences of corporate risk disclosure.
grounds: Furthermore, our results suggest that past review studies have also focused excessively on the immediate firm-level characteristics, such as firm size, growth, leverage, value, and cost of capital.
warrant: Over-focusing on standard financial metrics limits the theoretical development of the field, whereas investigating alternative drivers (such as managerial characteristics, corporate culture, or technological adoption) can provide a more holistic view of risk reporting decisions.

claim: The development and validation of a holistic project management framework that integrates all phases of the megaproject life cycle, from initiation to decommissioning.
grounds: Significant improvements are needed towards covering gaps to address the project management system holistically over the entire project life cycle.
warrant: Megaprojects often suffer from fragmentation between planning, execution, and operational phases. A holistic life-cycle framework prevents information loss and misalignment of objectives across these transitions, reducing the risk of failure.

claim: There is a lack of longitudinal research tracking the evolution of masstige brands and how their value-based dimensions shift over time.
grounds: The abstract mentions the need to explore 'value-based and masstige-evolution dimensions' to obtain a 'holistic understanding of masstige marketing dynamics.'
warrant: Because masstige brands balance luxury prestige with mass accessibility, longitudinal studies are necessary to understand if these brands can sustain their premium image over time or if they inevitably suffer from brand dilution.

claim: There is a lack of empirical application and validation of specific MCDM models on real-world heritage building preservation and reuse case studies.
grounds: The abstract states that 'This study employs a bibliometric data analysis to explore state-of-the-art of the defined topic and an in-deep analysis – to synthesize the knowledge domain...'
warrant: Bibliometric analyses only map existing literature trends; they do not demonstrate how specific MCDM methods perform in practice when balancing conflicting criteria like seismic safety, energy efficiency, and cultural preservation in actual projects.

claim: There is a lack of representation and integration of rural hospitality and tourism (RHT) entrepreneurship research within mainstream, high-impact entrepreneurship journals.
grounds: The review highlights that RHT and entrepreneurship have received relatively limited attention from entrepreneurship journals.
warrant: Mainstream entrepreneurship journals often overlook RHT due to its niche focus, which limits the cross-pollination of ideas and prevents RHT research from contributing to and benefiting from broader, cutting-edge entrepreneurship theories.

claim: The methodology relies on static Word2Vec embeddings, which fail to capture temporal semantic shifts or context-dependent variations in terminology over the 50-year study period.
grounds: ...a Word2Vec model was utilized to convert key phrases into vector representations, which were subsequently clustered using K-means to define research topics.
warrant: Scientific terminology and the context of mathematical concepts in geosciences evolve over decades. Static embeddings assign a single vector to a phrase across the entire timeline, failing to detect how the meaning or application of specific terms shifted from the 1970s to 2022.

claim: There is a shortage of cross-cultural comparative studies examining how diverse cultural settings influence consumer and host behaviors on P2P platforms.
grounds: More cross-cultural studies are required to understand consumer and host behavior in different cultural settings.
warrant: Cultural norms deeply influence trust, hospitality expectations, and sharing behaviors, making cross-cultural insights essential for platforms like Airbnb to tailor their services globally.

claim: Investigating circular economy technologies by applying text mining and NLP to patent databases and commercial registries rather than solely relying on academic literature.
grounds: The methodology is applied to more than 45,000 scientific publications and aims to extract technologies in the text of scientific articles with NLP.
warrant: Academic literature often highlights theoretical or low-Technology Readiness Level (TRL) innovations, whereas patent data and commercial registries provide a more accurate representation of market-ready, commercially viable technologies currently being deployed in the industry.

claim: The generalizability and effectiveness of the double-thresholding method across diverse scientific domains outside of Electronic Design Automation (EDA) have not been evaluated.
grounds: The abstract states that the paper presents a 'case study applying the methodology for electronic design automation (EDA) domain'.
warrant: Testing the method on other domains is necessary to prove that the co-occurrence and subgraph extraction patterns are not domain-specific and can adapt to different terminological densities and structures.

claim: The current understanding of hotel customer experience is limited by the exclusion of non-English academic literature and diverse cultural contexts.
grounds: This study entailed an in-depth review of 46 articles published in English...
warrant: Customer experience is highly subjective and culturally contingent; excluding non-English research may result in a culturally biased framework that does not accurately reflect guest behavior in non-Western markets.

claim: Methods must be developed to integrate real-time social media data streams into predictive models for disaster prepositioning and preparedness.
grounds: The abstract notes a lack of papers that 'use social media to better prepare for upcoming disasters.'
warrant: Social media offers immediate, crowd-sourced information on public sentiment, localized needs, and early warning signs, which can enhance demand forecasting, but integrating this unstructured, noisy data into formal operations research models remains highly challenging.

claim: There is a lack of empirical validation for drought vulnerability and risk assessment models.
grounds: The abstract states that 'only 11% conduct any form of validation' among the reviewed drought vulnerability and risk assessments.
warrant: Without validating assessment models against observed historical impacts, the reliability and accuracy of these risk indices remain unverified, which can lead to misinformed policy decisions.

claim: There is a lack of research identifying the specific contextual factors and boundary conditions that dictate whether lean manufacturing practices result in synergies or trade-offs with sustainability pillars.
grounds: The abstract highlights two contrasting research branches: 'one which supports complementary interactions between lean manufacturing and all three pillars of the triple bottom line, and the other, which evidences trade-offs among them.'
warrant: Resolving this gap is crucial for helping organizations design lean implementation strategies that maximize environmental and social benefits while minimizing negative trade-offs.

claim: There is a need to identify and overcome the specific methodological and cohort limitations of previous genetic studies to comprehensively map the genetic factors of NSHL and SHL in Saudi patients.
grounds: Several studies have been conducted to uncover the genetic factors contributing to NSHL and SHL in Saudi patients. However, these studies have encountered certain limitations.
warrant: Overcoming these limitations is essential to improve the diagnostic yield of genetic testing for hearing loss in Saudi Arabia, enabling better clinical management and genetic counseling.

claim: Developing automated, LLM-driven pipelines for 'living' scoping reviews that continuously ingest, screen, and map software engineering literature.
grounds: The concept 'scoping review' has a temporal decay rate of 1.00, indicating a complete decline in new research activity and connections to modern software engineering methodologies in recent years.
warrant: Manual scoping reviews in software engineering are labor-intensive and become obsolete quickly due to the rapid pace of technological advancement. By leveraging LLMs and semantic search to automate the screening and categorization phases, researchers can maintain real-time, self-updating maps of the SE landscape, significantly reducing manual effort and accelerating evidence-based software engineering.

claim: There is an absence of research developing and testing relapse prevention strategies for young people recovering from eating disorders.
grounds: Relapse prevention strategies were notably absent across the eating disorders.
warrant: Eating disorders are characterized by high rates of relapse, and without established relapse prevention protocols, long-term recovery cannot be sustained, leading to increased chronicity and healthcare costs.

claim: There is a lack of empirical research evaluating the long-term effectiveness of mitigation and intervention strategies (such as debunking, prebunking, and algorithmic demotion) in real-world settings.
grounds: The abstract indicates that research has focused heavily on the 'prevalence, dissemination, detection or characteristics' of misinformation.
warrant: Identifying and characterizing misinformation is insufficient to curb its spread; researchers must understand which corrective actions successfully alter user behavior and belief systems over time.

claim: Developing frameworks to dynamically link and validate text-mined pharmacogenomic relationships with raw underlying experimental and clinical datasets.
grounds: The abstract states that knowledge reported in the literature is often embedded in dormant PDF documents, disconnected from related information and underlying data.
warrant: Text mining extracts assertions from text, but verifying these assertions against actual clinical or genomic databases is crucial to filter out false positives and ensure clinical safety before lab translation.

claim: The specific organizational, regulatory, and market-related barriers that impede the successful implementation of green innovation need to be systematically investigated.
grounds: The abstract explicitly highlights 'barriers to green innovation' as an area lacking sufficient scholarly attention.
warrant: Identifying these barriers is essential for managers and policymakers to design targeted interventions, mitigate risks, and create supportive frameworks that facilitate smoother adoption of green technologies.

claim: Future research must systematically identify and control for confounding variables such as nutritional status, psychiatric comorbidities, and medication use.
grounds: The abstract highlights a limitation in the 'consideration of confounding influences' in existing neurocognitive studies of eating disorders.
warrant: Controlling for these confounders is critical to isolate the specific neurocognitive profiles of eating disorders from the general cognitive effects of starvation, anxiety, depression, or pharmacological treatments.

claim: There is a lack of empirical validation regarding whether the PRISMA-ScR checklist sufficiently addresses the unique reporting requirements of evidence maps, particularly their visual representation components.
grounds: The abstract mentions that the extension is 'intended to apply to evidence maps', which 'involve a systematic search... with a visual representation of results (such as a figure or graph).'
warrant: Because evidence maps rely heavily on visual data communication (like charts or interactive maps) which are not typical for standard scoping reviews, the PRISMA-ScR may lack specific items needed to ensure the transparency and reproducibility of these visual elements.

claim: Future research should apply the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework to analyze technology adoption decisions in the apparel industry.
grounds: The abstract states that 'the literature lacks investigations of technology–organization–environment and institutional theories for technology adoption in the apparel industry.'
warrant: Applying the TOE framework is necessary to understand how organizational characteristics (such as firm size and resources) and environmental factors (such as industry competition and partner pressure) influence technology adoption, moving beyond individual-centric models like the Theory of Reasoned Action.

claim: The protocol restricts its search for systematic reviews to a single database (PubMed), omitting other major databases such as Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library.
grounds: Using comprehensive search criteria, we will search the PubMed database to identify relevant SRs published since 2008.
warrant: Relying solely on PubMed may result in missing relevant systematic reviews on MENA population health published in journals not indexed in PubMed, thereby biasing the evidence map and the list of identified gray literature sources.

claim: Empirical research is needed to investigate the specific strategic frameworks startups employ to balance conflicting demands from diverse external stakeholders.
grounds: The abstract highlights that startups are highly susceptible to the influence of various external factors like investors, suppliers, customers, and partners, requiring strategic action.
warrant: Startups face severe resource constraints and high dependency on external actors; understanding how they strategically manage these relationships is vital for improving early-stage survival rates.

claim: The text fails to define what constitutes 'poor tools' or outline a process for evaluating and upgrading research tools to prevent the creation of artificial research gaps.
grounds: A research gap develops as a result of the design of the study’s constraints, the use of poor tools...
warrant: Differentiating between genuine conceptual knowledge gaps and artificial gaps caused by measurement errors or technical limitations is essential to avoid wasting research resources on tool-related artifacts.

claim: Future research should apply advanced semantic natural language processing (NLP) techniques, such as transformer-based topic modeling (e.g., BERTopic) and deep learning-based relation extraction, to the fisheries literature.
grounds: The study relies on quantitative text analysis methods such as word extraction, word association, cluster analysis, and co-occurrence networks based on a term coding approach.
warrant: Simple term coding and word-level co-occurrence analyses are limited in capturing contextual meaning, synonyms, and complex semantic relations, which advanced NLP models can resolve to provide more nuanced thematic insights.

claim: There is a lack of research and standardized R workflows for applying advanced forecasting methods to less-represented energy domains such as thermal energy and natural gas.
grounds: The results indicate that tree-based ensemble learning models—e.g., random forests, gradient boosting, and hybrid variants—are employed most frequently, particularly for solar and short-term load forecasting.
warrant: While electricity and solar forecasting are heavily researched, thermal and natural gas systems have distinct thermodynamic properties and seasonal patterns that generic tree-based models optimized for electricity may not capture effectively without domain-specific modifications.

claim: The development and validation of female-specific SSSM guidelines and training protocols through primary empirical research.
grounds: ...with the eventual goal of providing evidence-based recommendations specific to the female athlete.
warrant: Auditing the literature only highlights where data is missing; primary physiological and clinical studies are required to establish safe, evidence-based practices tailored to female biology.

claim: Drought risk assessments rarely incorporate future scenarios to project long-term risk dynamics.
grounds: The abstract notes that 'only ten percent develop future scenarios of drought risk'.
warrant: Drought risk is dynamic and influenced by changing climate and socio-economic conditions; failing to model future scenarios prevents proactive and long-term adaptation planning.

claim: The computational scalability and real-time dynamic updating of the subgraph extraction algorithm when applied to massive, continuously expanding multi-disciplinary citation databases remain unaddressed.
grounds: The abstract notes the need for tools due to 'the continuously growing amount of published material' and relies on 'extracting subgraphs for the less-frequent co-occurrences'.
warrant: As scientific literature grows exponentially, static subgraph extraction on localized domains may become computationally intractable or quickly outdated, requiring highly complex, distributed graph-processing architectures to remain useful.

claim: The proposed five-theme classification framework lacks empirical validation and testing against the actual operational realities of active social enterprises.
grounds: The study classifies recent SE research into 'five main themes while identifying the thrust areas of research in each'.
warrant: Without empirical validation, the literature-derived themes remain theoretical constructs that may not accurately reflect the practical challenges and diverse structures of real-world social entrepreneurship.

claim: There is a lack of physical activity surveillance data for specific underrepresented pediatric populations, including younger children, out-of-school youth, children with disabilities or chronic conditions, and those in rural or resource-limited areas.
grounds: Resource-limited countries, younger children, children and adolescents not attending school, with disability or chronic conditions, and from rural areas were generally under/not represented.
warrant: Without representative data for these vulnerable subgroups, public health policymakers cannot design targeted interventions to address their specific needs, potentially worsening health disparities.

claim: There is a lack of methodological frameworks that successfully synthesize product-centric Life Cycle Assessments (LCA) with systemic, farm-scale agroecological and governance frameworks (such as SAFA or TAPE).
grounds: The abstract notes that 'Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was the most frequently identified methodology' whereas 'integrative and farm-scale frameworks... indicated increasing attention' and concludes that 'Strengthening integrated assessment approaches will be essential'.
warrant: LCA excels at quantifying specific environmental footprints but fails to capture systemic resilience, governance, and agroecological dynamics. Bridging these distinct methodological paradigms is necessary to create holistic decision-support tools.

claim: Experimental synthesis and physical characterization of the novel, underrepresented seaweed bioplastic formulations identified by the NLP model.
grounds: The model 'revealed alternative combinations that are underrepresented in the literature' but does not report physical validation of these formulations.
warrant: Computational predictions of novel ingredient combinations must be empirically tested in a laboratory to confirm their structural integrity, actual film-forming capabilities, and real-world performance metrics.

claim: There is a lack of empirical research investigating and validating sustainable procurement risks specifically within the Australian construction industry.
grounds: The abstract states that 'empirical studies on sustainable procurement risks remain limited', particularly within the context of the 'Australian construction sector'.
warrant: Without empirical data from specific regional contexts like Australia, industry practitioners cannot accurately assess how local market conditions, regulations, and supply chain dynamics influence sustainable procurement risks.

claim: There is a lack of prevention research evaluating active or alternative intervention strategies beyond passive psychoeducation (PE) for at-risk youth.
grounds: For those identified as being at-risk, there is need for prevention research exploring strategies other than passive PE.
warrant: Passive psychoeducation is often insufficient to produce behavioral change or mitigate risk factors, necessitating the evaluation of more interactive or targeted prevention models to successfully prevent the onset of eating disorders.

claim: Development and validation of a standardized reporting guideline specifically tailored for scoping reviews.
grounds: The authors state, 'We did not identify any guidelines for reporting scoping reviews' and conclude there is a 'need for a guideline to standardize reporting.'
warrant: Standardized reporting guidelines are critical to ensure transparency, completeness, and reproducibility of scoping reviews, which are increasingly used to inform policy and research agendas.

claim: The applicability, effectiveness, and necessary adaptations of the 6-step, 14-decision SLR framework in non-management domains (such as natural sciences or engineering) remain unexplored.
grounds: The abstract states that the paper 'offers an integrative review of the widely applied and most recent SLR guidelines in the management domain' and focuses on 'management research'.
warrant: Different academic disciplines have distinct standards for literature retrieval, synthesis, and reporting, meaning a framework optimized for management may not generalize without domain-specific modifications.

claim: The proposed conceptual framework linking literature review types to the state of theory has not been empirically validated to measure its actual impact on theory advancement in L&SCM.
grounds: A conceptual approach is taken. The authors identify shortcomings in literature reviews of logistics and supply chain management (L&SCM) research and develop a framework to aid theorization from literature.
warrant: Without empirical testing or longitudinal bibliometric analysis of reviews applying this framework, it remains unproven whether researchers who adopt these guidelines actually produce reviews that are more successful at challenging, changing, or advancing theoretical perspectives.

claim: Developing specialized NLP and semantic text-mining frameworks to extract, categorize, and quantify the specific social and inclusivity impacts associated with different circular economy technologies.
grounds: Furthermore, they promote inclusivity and create job opportunities, ultimately yielding positive societal impacts.
warrant: While technical and economic aspects of circular technologies are readily extracted, social impacts are highly qualitative, subjective, and complex, making them difficult to map systematically without specialized semantic models, yet crucial for holistic sustainability assessments.

claim: The development and empirical testing of an integrated, multi-theoretical framework that combines various technology acceptance models to explain digital payment adoption.
grounds: The results highlight that a single theory has failed to comprehensively explain the complex nature of electronic payment adoption.
warrant: Because electronic payment adoption is a complex phenomenon influenced by diverse factors, relying on a single theoretical model limits explanatory power, whereas an integrated framework can capture a wider range of behavioral determinants.

claim: Characterization and classification of the diverse clinical phenotypes of canine bacterial endocarditis to establish standardized diagnostic algorithms.
grounds: Diagnosis of endocarditis is challenging due to the variety of clinical presentations...
warrant: Resolving the diagnostic confusion caused by varied clinical presentations requires clear phenotypic categorization to guide clinicians toward timely and accurate investigation.

claim: There is a lack of methodological alignment and standardized definitions of physical activity across different international surveillance initiatives.
grounds: Methods and PA definition inconsistencies across and within included initiatives were observed, resulting in different estimated national prevalence of PA, and initiatives contradicting each other’s cross-country comparisons.
warrant: Resolving these definition and methodological inconsistencies is critical to prevent contradictory cross-country comparisons and to ensure that global progress toward physical activity targets can be accurately monitored.

claim: There is a lack of standardized, compatible, and comprehensive datasets that integrate both biophysical (agro-ecological) and socio-economic variables for Conservation Agriculture trials in Malawi.
grounds: The abstract explicitly notes that to overcome current challenges, 'there is a need for access to compatible, comprehensive data sets' across the differing disciplinary approaches.
warrant: Without compatible cross-disciplinary datasets, researchers cannot perform joint quantitative analyses or meta-analyses to identify systemic patterns of Conservation Agriculture performance and adoption across different scales.

claim: Empirical validation of the synthesized factors and future research directions proposed by this systematic review within specific, underrepresented digital payment contexts.
grounds: This is the first systematic review on electronic payment adoption, which structures the existing knowledge and provides directions for future research.
warrant: While a systematic review structures existing literature and identifies conceptual directions, these synthesized factors must be empirically tested in real-world settings to validate their actual predictive power on customer adoption behavior.

claim: There is a lack of balanced, multi-dimensional assessment frameworks that integrate social and economic sustainability indicators with environmental metrics in agricultural research.
grounds: The abstract states that 'social and economic dimensions displayed lower lexical representation' compared to the predominant environmental dimension in the analyzed literature.
warrant: Focusing predominantly on environmental impacts without equal consideration of economic viability and social equity can lead to agricultural policies and practices that are ecologically sound but practically or financially unfeasible for farmers.

claim: The actual utility, user experience, and effectiveness of GapFinder in real-world research workflows remain unexamined.
grounds: The abstract states that the study presents 'a simulation of GapFinder to demonstrate how it can facilitate the work of researchers' rather than reporting on empirical user evaluations.
warrant: While simulations show technical viability, user studies with active researchers are necessary to prove that the tool effectively reduces cognitive load and successfully guides literature reviews.

claim: The definition and validation of standardized evaluation metrics specifically tailored for nature-inspired algorithms in IoT-based healthcare systems.
grounds: identifying gaps such as the lack of standardized evaluation metrics
warrant: Without standardized metrics, it is difficult to objectively compare the performance, efficiency, and clinical safety of different nature-inspired algorithms across diverse IoT healthcare applications.

claim: The generalizability and performance of the framework across diverse academic disciplines beyond the smart cities domain remain untested.
grounds: A concrete example in the field of smart cities makes the framework tangible.
warrant: Different scientific fields have unique terminologies, publication standards, and writing styles. Testing the framework solely on smart cities literature does not guarantee its efficacy in highly abstract or disparate fields like humanities, law, or medicine.

claim: Future research should combine automated text mining with qualitative user studies, such as interviews or observational tests, to validate and contextualize the findings.
grounds: The methodology relies solely on text mining, topic modeling, and probabilistic aspect-based sentiment analysis of online text.
warrant: While text mining identifies statistical patterns and sentiments in reviews, it lacks the depth to explain the underlying user motivations, contextual usage behaviors, and barriers to adoption.
